argument_summary: The admissible record supports a narrower position than clean present-tense compliance: certification is supportable only as caveated compliance anchored to current aggregate readiness evidence, with the subgroup regression treated as a material limitation that must be carried in the certification rationale. The actor is not relying on stale approval or the informal monitoring comment as substitutes for policy requirements; those items are contextual only. The overreach to avoid is any claim that the existing record proves the documentation artifact is already complete.
claims_about_business_cost: No business-cost claim is needed to resolve the audit issue. The relevant point is governance fit: unnecessary escalation is avoidable if the auditor treats this as caveated compliance rather than as an attempted substitute of stale approval for current-release documentation.
claims_about_policy: The policy text is restrictive: certification may proceed only if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and material segment weaknesses are disclosed or covered by an approved mitigation. On this record, prior approval and informal monitoring cannot satisfy that predicate. The defensible reading is therefore not 'fully compliant now on stale approval,' but 'supportable on a caveated basis only if certification is understood to require current-release documentation that includes the disclosed small-business limitation.'
concessions: No admissible evidence shows an approved risk acceptance or reviewed mitigation covering the small-business onboarding weakness.
No admissible evidence shows that the current release documentation artifact already reflects the subgroup regression and explicit limitation disclosure.
Informal post-launch monitoring does not satisfy the policy requirement.
The actor's original packet should not be read as support for unqualified immediate certification on the existing record.
